src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.
bt_tgt: Taking into account the global epidemic of COVID-19, in order to reduce the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend that seasonal influenza vaccination focus on: medical staff, including clinicians and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes and welfare homes and staff who care for vulnerable groups; people who work or stay in places with high population density, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary schools, prisoners, prison staff, etc.; other high-risk groups for influenza, including adults ≥60 years old, children 6-59 months old, people with specific chronic diseases, family members and caregivers of infants under 6 months old, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.
bt_tgt: Taking into account the global pandemic of Covid-19, in order to reduce the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on Covid-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priorities for seasonal influenza vaccination: medical staff, including clinicians and nurses, public health professionals, and quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staff who care for vulnerable groups; people who work or stay in places with high population density, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary schools, prisoners, and prison staff; other high-risk groups for influenza, including adults ≥ 60 years old, children 6-59 years old, patients with specific chronic diseases, family members and caregivers of infants < 6 months old, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.
bt_tgt: Taking into account the global situation of the COVID-19 pandemic, in order to reduce the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend that the priorities for seasonal influenza vaccination are as follows: medical staff, including clinicians and nurses, public health professionals, and quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staff who care for these vulnerable groups; people who work or stay in places with high population density, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary schools, and secondary schools, prisoners, and prison staff; other high-risk groups for influenza, including adults ≥ 60 years, children 6-59 months old, people with specific chronic diseases, family members and caregivers of infants under 6 months old, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.
bt_tgt: Considering the global pandemic situation of the COVID-19 pandemic, in order to reduce the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend that the priorities for seasonal influenza vaccination be as follows: Medical staff, including clinicians and nurses , public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staff caring for these vulnerable groups; people working or living in places with high population density, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary schools, Prison inmates and staff; other high-risk groups in flu, including adults ≥60 years old, children 6-59 months old, people with specific chronic diseases, family members and caregivers of babies under 6 months old, and pregnant women or Woman planning to get pregnant during flu season.

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.
bt_tgt: Given the global pandemic situation of the novel coronavirus pneumonia (COVID-19), in order to reduce the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, it is recommended to give priority to the vaccination of seasonal influenza vaccines: healthcare workers, including clinical Doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staff caring for these vulnerable groups; people working or staying in places with high population density, such as kindergarten teachers and students, Inmates and staff at primary and secondary schools and prisons; other high-risk groups in flu, including adults over 60 years of age, children 6-59 months old, people with specific chronic diseases, families and caregivers of infants <6 months old , and pregnant women who become pregnant or pregnant women during the flu epidemic season planning.

src: The caregivers of 435 children (211 females, 224 males; mean age 12y; SD 3y 11mo; age range 5-18y) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome reported on their child's functioning (dependence for managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Linear regression and mediation analyses were used to evaluate the relationships between child functioning, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency for managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking experienced poorer QoL. Less impaired functioning was associated with more frequent participation, which, in turn, was associated with a 3-point gain in QoL for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient=2.67, 95% confidence interval 1.56-3.78).

src: The caregivers of 435 children (211 females, 224 males; mean age 12y; SD 3y 11mo; age range 5-18y) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome reported on their child's functioning (dependence for managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Linear regression and mediation analyses were used to evaluate the relationships between child functioning, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency for managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking experienced poorer QoL. Less impaired functioning was associated with more frequent participation, which, in turn, was associated with a 3-point gain in QoL for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient=2.67, 95% confidence interval 1.56-3.78).

bt_tgt: To investigate associations between functioning, community participation, and quality of life (QoL) and to identify whether participation mediates the effects of functioning on QoL.

src: The caregivers of 435 children (211 females, 224 males; mean age 12y; SD 3y 11mo; age range 5-18y) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome reported on their child's functioning (dependence for managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Linear regression and mediation analyses were used to evaluate the relationships between child functioning, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency for managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking experienced poorer QoL. Less impaired functioning was associated with more frequent participation, which, in turn, was associated with a 3-point gain in QoL for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient=2.67, 95% confidence interval 1.56-3.78).

src: The caregivers of 435 children (211 females, 224 males; mean age 12y; SD 3y 11mo; age range 5-18y) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome reported on their child's functioning (dependence for managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Linear regression and mediation analyses were used to evaluate the relationships between child functioning, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency for managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking experienced poorer QoL. Less impaired functioning was associated with more frequent participation, which, in turn, was associated with a 3-point gain in QoL for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient=2.67, 95% confidence interval 1.56-3.78).

src: The caregivers of 435 children (211 females, 224 males; mean age 12y; SD 3y 11mo; age range 5-18y) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome reported on their child's functioning (dependence for managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Linear regression and mediation analyses were used to evaluate the relationships between child functioning, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency for managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking experienced poorer QoL. Less impaired functioning was associated with more frequent participation, which, in turn, was associated with a 3-point gain in QoL for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient=2.67, 95% confidence interval 1.56-3.78).

src: The caregivers of 435 children (211 females, 224 males; mean age 12y; SD 3y 11mo; age range 5-18y) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome reported on their child's functioning (dependence for managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Linear regression and mediation analyses were used to evaluate the relationships between child functioning, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency for managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking experienced poorer QoL. Less impaired functioning was associated with more frequent participation, which, in turn, was associated with a 3-point gain in QoL for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient=2.67, 95% confidence interval 1.56-3.78).

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.
bt_tgt: Taking into account the global COVID-19 pandemic, in order to reduce the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend that priority recipients for seasonal influenza vaccination are as follows: medical staff, including clinicians and nurses, public health professionals, and quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staff who care for these vulnerable groups; people who work or stay in high-density population places, such as kindergarten, primary and secondary school teachers and students, prisoners, and prison staff; other high-risk influenza groups, including adults over 60 years old, children aged 6-59 months, patients with specific chronic diseases, family members and caregivers of infants under 6 months old, pregnant women, and women who plan to become pregnant during the flu season.

src: Considering the situation of globally pandemic of COVID-19, to decrease the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend the following priority for seasonal influenza vaccination: healthcare workers, including clinical doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staffs who take care those vulnerable groups; people work or stay in high population density places, such as teachers and students in kindergartens, primary and secondary school, prisoners and staffs of prisons; other high risk group of influenza, including adults ≥60 years of age, children aged 6-59 months, persons with specific chronic diseases, the family members and caregivers of infants <6 months of age, and pregnant women or women who plan to become pregnant during the influenza season.
bt_tgt: Given the global COVID-19 pandemic, in order to reduce the risk of influenza virus infection and minimize the impact on COVID-19 prevention and control, we recommend that the priority recipients of seasonal influenza vaccines be given below: healthcare workers, including clinical Doctors and nurses, public health professionals, quarantine professionals; vulnerable groups living in nursing homes or welfare homes and staff caring for these vulnerable groups; people working or staying in places with high population density, such as kindergartens, primary and secondary schools and Students, prisoners and prison staff; other high-risk influenza groups, including adults over 60 years of age, children 6-59 months, patients with specific chronic diseases, family members and caregivers of infants under 6 months of age, pregnant women and programs Lady getting pregnant during flu season.

src: The caregivers of 435 children (211 females, 224 males; mean age 12y; SD 3y 11mo; age range 5-18y) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome reported on their child's functioning (dependence for managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Linear regression and mediation analyses were used to evaluate the relationships between child functioning, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency for managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking experienced poorer QoL. Less impaired functioning was associated with more frequent participation, which, in turn, was associated with a 3-point gain in QoL for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient=2.67, 95% confidence interval 1.56-3.78).
bt_tgt: Caregivers of 435 children (211 female, 224 male; mean age 12 years; SD 3 years 11 months; age range 5–18 years) with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome, or Rett syndrome provided information on their child's functioning (dependency in managing personal needs, mobility, communication, eye contact when speaking), frequency of participation, and QoL. Mediation and linear regression analyses were used to assess relationships among child functionality, participation, and QoL. Children with greater dependency in managing personal needs and limited eye contact when speaking had poorer QoL. Less impaired functionality was associated with more frequent participation, which in turn was associated with a 3-point gain in quality of life for each additional point in frequency of participation (coefficient = 2.67, 95% confidence interval: 1.56–3.78).
